svg.title: The odds of a swarm
svg.desc: Chart of 1 − (1 − p)^n showing that many cheap low-probability attempts sum to high overall success odds, with labeled combinations such as p equal to 1 percent over 100 attempts reaching 63 percent.
svg.text: Illustrative independent attempts with equal success probability p · not an empirical forecast

g.text: failure is per-attempt; success is per-swarm
Victim billed when access is stolen
Each attempt has the same success probability p
Shared failure modes can reduce effective trials
Defenses can change p and limit n
Repeated attempts can accumulate risk; independence is an assumption, not a guarantee.
Correlated failures, rate limits, detection, and defensive automation change real outcomes. These curves are not measured attack success rates.

svg.text: No Fate But What We Bill · figure 3 · 1 − (1 − p)^n
